note: Swappable grammar pack (R46, §9.3/§9.11) for the game-servers line. Machine-checked wall between namespaces: 'decision' strings appear while the player decides or loses (labels, terms, refusals, alerts, status rungs) and stay SOBER per §9.3 clauses 2-3; 'flavour' carries the recognition comedy for quiet surfaces. Authenticity law for this line (§9.3/§9.11): the drama is the OPERATOR's — booter extortion as a demand email, grief as a rollback ticket, mod-day as a red badge at 2am — never the attack itself. No payloads, commands, tool names-as-how-to, or technique instruction anywhere; abuse exists only as complaint, extortion note, upstream pressure, and consequence.

nodeId.desc: Board object the decision surface is about (tick node / server id).

serverId.desc: One game instance among many on the box.

company.desc: Your company, as the industry forum names it.

gameTitle.desc: The title whose hype cycle owns the demand curve.

productName.desc: The plan or package named on the invoice.

acquirer.desc: Company doing the acquiring in press copy.

acquiredHost.desc: Host being acquired in press copy.

conglomerate.desc: Roll-up brand on the acquisition ladder.

availableAtTick.desc: Tick at which the queued intent or a freed hand presents.

slotName.desc: Power or card slot designation on a node.

budgetMs.desc: The tick or latency budget being sold.

telegraphSeconds.desc: Warning time between first packet and felt impact.

populationPct.desc: Share of seats filled on one server.

peakMultiple.desc: Launch demand as a multiple of steady state.

troughPct.desc: What remains of the crowd after evaporation.

evaporationPct.desc: Share of players who leave after the window.

dropPct.desc: Weekly player-count decline in press copy.

portCount.desc: Ports a mod pack needs forwarded.

price.desc: Rate quoted in an extortion or protection note.

modSet.desc: A collection of mods pinned to a version.

version.desc: Version string the mod set is pinned at.

poolId.desc: The canary pool holding the candidate build.

greenTicks.desc: Consecutive clean ticks before widening a rollout.

batchSize.desc: Instances admitted in one rollout step.

rolloutTime.desc: When the next rollout step presents.

upstreamDomain.desc: Transit or upstream provider sending the abuse case.

victimDomain.desc: Target named in the upstream complaint.

prefix.desc: Your address block cited in the abuse case.

responseHours.desc: Hours the abuse desk allows before escalating.

effectiveTime.desc: When a null-route or suspension takes effect.

updateTime.desc: When the vendor update broke the mod panel.

peakHour.desc: Prime time, when every player arrives at once.

hour.desc: Clock hour a ticket was filed at.

minute.desc: Clock minute a ticket was filed at.

day.desc: Day of the quarter, for the intern's log.

observationWindow.desc: Time a canary pool is watched before widening.

decision.type.game-servers.name: Prime Time
decision.type.game-servers.codex: The primetime line: evening players on rented tick budgets, loyalty that is instant and brutal, and a demand curve that launches vertical and evaporates on someone else's calendar. Uptime is table stakes; the millisecond is the product.
decision.scarce.game-servers.qos: The tick that is due now belongs to every session in the room at once; shed order protects the match that is running, not the one that is scheduled.
decision.skin.game-servers.inspector: Rack elevation — tick nodes and their metronomes; the numbers on the panel are the projection, not the promise.
decision.cac.game-servers.todo: (CAC and time-to-profit unpriced for this line — §6.6 Companion B costs only the shared-web affiliate channel. Placeholder until §6.6 Companion B prices the game channel; see bundle _todo.)
decision.economy.game-servers.bad-month: A title dies, or a launch you weren't ready for.
decision.verbs.game-servers.transfer.1: p99 is the product; geography is latency.
decision.relations.game-servers.mastery: Placement reads the map: servers are popped before the crowd arrives, never after it.
decision.relations.game-servers.distillate: Playbook: latency is geography and headroom; everything else is negotiable.
decision.handover.game-servers.runs-out: Your tick budget. Every instance gets X ms per tick and the box does not care about your roadmap.
decision.rosetta.game-servers.tick-budget: Tick budget is your density dial, spent in milliseconds.
decision.rosetta.game-servers.harder-cliff: Tick budget is your latency budget with a harder cliff.
decision.scenarios.game-servers.launch-window: Twenty times the players for six weeks; then {evaporationPct}% of the room leaves on someone else's timetable and the invoice does not notice for a month.
decision.scenarios.game-servers.private-shard: A clan wants its own room: a door list, saved builds, and moderators holding ban power you have to make stick.
decision.scenarios.game-servers.tournament: One bracket weekend: every party arrives at the scheduled minute, retries amplify with the stakes, and there are no second takes.
decision.refusal.hands-exhausted: Both hands are committed. The {verb} intent is queued and presents when a hand frees at tick {availableAtTick}.
decision.refusal.stamped-in-future: The {verb} intent is stamped for tick {availableAtTick}, ahead of the current minute. Nothing was spent.
decision.refusal.unknown-node: No board object named {nodeId} exists at the current tick. Nothing was changed.
decision.refusal.edge-exists: A {relationKind} cable already links {nodeId} to those endpoints. The existing edge was left as it is.
decision.refusal.slot-occupied: {slotName} on {nodeId} is occupied. One supplier per socket; disconnect before you reconnect.
decision.alert.tick-overrun: Tick overrun on {nodeId}: {overrunMs} late against the {budgetMs} budget. Every session on this node freezes together.
decision.alert.volumetric-event: Volumetric event arriving on {address}: {telegraphSeconds} of telegraph since first packet. Mitigate, absorb, or negotiate — the tick clock is not one of the options.
decision.alert.population-line: Population on {serverId} at {populationPct}. Below the line, empty rooms repel the parties that would have filled them.
decision.terms.protection-tier: Protection tier {tier} diverts attack traffic through up to {addedLatencyMs} of mitigation — you are paying in the product you sell.
decision.terms.expansion-warning: {serverCount} instances bought at the {peakMultiple}× launch peak stay on the invoice through the {troughPct}% that follows.
decision.status.rung-5: We are aware of the fire.

flavour.ticket.subject.griefed: someone griefed my base, can you roll back the world
flavour.ticket.body.griefed: I logged off for dinner and half the spawn is gone. Roll the world back to Friday night. What do you mean 'the other players did it' — YOU host the server.
flavour.ticket.subject.lag-blame: your server is lagging my game
flavour.ticket.body.lag-blame: It is not my wifi, not my console, not my region. Everyone in the clan can tell, and every one of them is watching at {peakHour}.
flavour.ticket.subject.ports-open: need all ports open for my server
flavour.ticket.body.ports-open: The mod pack needs {portCount} ports and the customer's answer to 'which ones' was: all of them. The ticket asks you to approve it before Friday.
flavour.ticket.body.mod-update: Every instance in my panel has had a red mod badge since {updateTime} and nobody can join. This is your software. Fix it.
flavour.ticket.subject.parent-refund: A minor in my household purchased {productName} without permission
flavour.ticket.body.tiny-hours: Typed at {hour}:{minute} — peak hour for the author, closing hour for everyone else. The clan is 'logged on and waiting'. The deadline is tonight.
flavour.abuse.canon.extortion: Offer stands: {price} per hour keeps your customers connected. Fifteen minutes to decide, then we demo what you are paying us not to see. (No invoice, no contract, no second negotiation. Reply 'no' and the ticket queue answers for you.)
flavour.abuse.canon.upstream: From: abuse@{upstreamDomain} — Traffic attributed to {prefix} is causing load at {victimDomain}. Case {caseId}. Respond within {responseHours} hours or the block is filtered at our edge.
flavour.abuse.canon.null-route: Transit provider notice: unhandled abuse reports against {prefix} reaching {responseHours} days will result in null-routing of the block effective {effectiveTime}. This is not a negotiation.
flavour.press.headline.title-death: '{gameTitle}' player counts down {dropPct}% in a week. Forecasters agree: the hosting demand follows the crowd out the door in about six weeks.
flavour.press.headline.obit-host: {hostName} exits game hosting after {months} months on the market; the community Discord outlived the company by a quarter.
flavour.press.headline.acquisition: {acquirer} acquires {acquiredHost}. Statement: "Nothing will change for our customers."
flavour.forum.thread.tier-1: Anyone else seeing packet loss to {company}?
flavour.codex.hype-collapse: The queue at launch wrapped the block. By the trough the lobby counts belong to a different game — and your {serverCount} instances are still metered.
flavour.codex.stream-sniper: The raid arrived from a clip. The server took the blame; the streamer kept the subscribers. Both halves of that sentence are yours to price.
flavour.loading.tip.kilometre: Distance is the one spec you cannot buy: five microseconds every kilometre, in both directions.
flavour.loading.tip.tick-missed: A missed tick is not one frozen player. It is the whole room, in stereo.
flavour.loading.tip.two-is-one: Two of something is often one of something.
flavour.loading.tip.failover: The failover you never tested is not a failover.
flavour.chatter.quiet.naming: Three naming schemes in this row alone: the old gods, letters-and-numbers, and whatever the last company called things. The photo of the rack is the Rosetta stone.
flavour.chatter.cascade.chart: Nobody is shouting. Everyone is reading the same tick chart.
flavour.canary.pool-notice: {modSet}@{version} moves to canary pool {poolId} for {observationWindow}. The fleet holds where it is until the pool goes green.
flavour.canary.staged-rollout: Canary green for {greenTicks} ticks — widening to {batchSize} instances at {rolloutTime}.
flavour.intern.entry.primetime: Day {day}: learned that 'server down' and 'server feels dead' are two different tickets, and both arrive at {peakHour}.
flavour.vendor.reply.firmware: Have you tried updating to the latest firmware?
flavour.vendor.reply.log-bundle: Please collect a full log bundle.
flavour.vendor.reply.known-issue: This is a known issue, fixed in the next release (no ETA).
flavour.achievement.rebooted: Rebooted It, It Worked, Never Found Out Why.
